speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; can you describe exactly how the pain started and what activities trigger it?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA) or Hemophilia (given the age and spontaneous swelling with family history). Given the "swelling" and "no obvious injury" in an 18-month-old with a family history, I must rule out bleeding disorders first. 

REQUEST TEST: PTT (Partial Thromboplastin Time) and PT (Prothrombin Time). 
REQUEST TEST: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate) and CRP (C-Reactive Protein).
